## User clarification

The user specifies that final coordinates must contain no negative numbers. The follow-up corrects the speech transcription: crossing may have equal values, not necessarily an increment by one. Interpret this as equality of relevant address values, not physical waiting, paused time, or the prohibition of existing reverse operations. Six positive-axis address fields remain the design target; inactive fields may be zero when decoding remains complete.

## Exact interface conditions

Let E_q:C_q->A_q subset N_0^6 be a proposed injective local encoding, with inverse D_q on its valid image. The full implementation must identify the chart from metadata or an unambiguous code pattern. No specific complete six-field sector atlas is claimed to have been constructed here.

For the same Cell represented on a chart overlap, H_rq=E_r D_q and D_r H_rq=D_q. There is no general +1 term. When H_rq is a permitted coordinate permutation, H_rq(a)=P a preserves nonnegativity and simply relocates unchanged values. This is valid only when the chart decoders satisfy D_r P=D_q on the relevant domain. Moving a value between fixed native axes without this identity is not thereby a legal chart change.

For an actual native step F:P->Q, the address transition is K_rq=E_r F D_q. A field or layer observer lambda can satisfy lambda(E_q(P))=lambda(E_r(Q)) while P and Q are distinct. Equality of an observed number does not imply zero displacement, absence of an event, or zero elapsed time. The full global identity must still distinguish distinct Cells; identical final six digits for different Cells require additional disambiguating chart information, or else the encoding is not injective.

For any observed address statistic lambda, the claim that every relevant transition raises it by one requires the separate law lambda K=lambda+1. Nonnegative output and crossing a display boundary do not imply this law. Equality is the distinct possible law lambda K=lambda on the specified transition domain. Neither law is assumed universally.

## BRC and preservation boundary

REUSE_APPLIED: the prior reversible-address/labeled-walk theorem and V2 alias normalization. Chart changes of one Cell are representation operations, not extra physical edges. Real edges remain counted even when their endpoints share a layer/value. Preserve their actual identity, order, ports and weights. Do not add a fake step to explain a code increment or erase a real step because a displayed number stays equal. This applies the existing BRC carrier; it introduces no new tool or signed/phase interpretation.

The previous two-sided gap codec and its p+m-1 distance law remain conditional records, not governing formulas for the intended six-field nonnegative sector encoding. Likewise, the all-zero numeric vector must not be equated with a display origin without a declared code-domain rule. Do not erase common depth or unobserved native data by calling it inactive.

## Scope and next exact obligation

Record the target as: final digits nonnegative; inactive fields zero only losslessly; equal-value boundary transfer allowed; no automatic +1; stable full Cell identity and original physical transitions preserved.

The next concrete model obligation is a table of adjacent-chart valid domains, decode maps, and actual boundary correspondences. Verify nonnegativity, inverse/roundtrip consistency, same-Cell equality for recharting, and native-edge consistency for motion separately. This clarification fixes the target; it does not select an unsupported boundary formula or prove the final atlas compatible.

No new numerical test, production change, Lean proof, physical waiting rule, P000 edit, or worldview modification was performed in this clarification.
